findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() uses unwrap() on fallible I/O
findings.failure_mode: Corrupted, missing, or unreadable metric file panics the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and propagate the I/O error with ?

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side effect / I/O in a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: The function has logging side effects that are not expressed in the type signature, making it impossible to compose purely and causing uncontrolled stdout output in tests and production
findings.fix: Remove the println! entirely. If metrics/logging are needed, pass an observer callback or return a log event in the result type

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: If a line has no comma, parts.len() == 1 and subsequent parts[1] access will panic at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get exactly two parts, returning an error for malformed lines

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() + indexed access instead of split_once for a two-field CSV line
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a Vec<String> for all fields even though only two are needed. If the line has more or fewer than 2 comma-separated values, indexing [0] and [1] is either wasteful or panics
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract the name and value parts in one operation, then trim and parse only those two

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() uses unwrap() on fallible numeric parsing
findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric content in the value field (e.g., 'abc', empty string, floating point) panics instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (or a domain error enum) and propagate parse failure with ? or map_err

findings.problem: Lossy cast as u16 on a u32 parse result
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 65536..=u32::MAX silently truncate to u16::MAX, producing incorrect records without any error or warning
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) to return a typed error when the value exceeds u16::MAX

findings.problem: load_metrics mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!) with data parsing and validation in a single function
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be tested purely (unit tests would need filesystem access and capture stdout). Parsing logic is coupled to I/O side effects, violating the functional core / imperative shell separation
findings.fix: Split into: (1) a pure fn parse_records(lines: impl Iterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> in the core, and (2) a shell fn load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, AppError> that handles I/O and delegates to the parser

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 instead of typed domain newtypes
findings.failure_mode: No type-level guarantee that name is non-empty or value is in valid range. Any code can construct an invalid Record, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: Introduce a non-empty Name newtype with a fallible constructor, and validate value range in the constructor or use a domain error enum to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: load_metrics returns Vec<Record> with no error type, forcing unwrap/panic on every failure path
findings.failure_mode: All failure modes (file not found, read error, parse error, invalid format, out-of-range value) collapse into a single panic with no way for callers to distinguish or handle them
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum (e.g., MetricsError { Io(std::io::Error), Parse { line: usize, field: &'static str, reason: String } }) and return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricsError>

findings.problem: Collects every line field into Vec<String> unnecessarily; no try_reserve or bounded capacity handling
findings.failure_mode: Wastes heap allocation per line. If the capacity were bounded, allocation failure would be silently ignored rather than handled as a recoverable error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and avoid Vec allocation entirely. If Vec is ever needed for batch operations, use try_reserve with Allocation error handling

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to validate performance characteristics of load_metrics
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmark evidence, allocation patterns (per-line Vec<String>, String allocations for trim+clone) cannot be verified as acceptable for the intended workload size
findings.fix: Add a cargo bench benchmark that measures parse throughput for representative file sizes (small, medium, large) to establish baselines and detect regressions

findings.problem: No profiler evidence or flamegraph provided for the metrics loading path
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm that hot path allocations (String::trim, String::to_string, Vec collect) are the actual bottleneck vs. I/O latency
findings.fix: Run cargo flamegraph or perf record on load_metrics with realistic input to identify the true hot path before optimizing

findings.problem: No allocation audit (e.g., heaptrack, jemalloc stats) for the hot path
findings.failure_mode: Hidden O(n) per-line allocations may cause excessive GC pressure or heap fragmentation at scale
findings.fix: Use heaptrack or jemalloc profiling to measure per-line allocation count and total heap usage

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence: no miri, clippy, or cargo test run to validate correctness of the reviewed code
findings.failure_mode: Static review alone cannot confirm the absence of data races, UB, or that clippy has no additional warnings on this crate
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo miri test if applicable to produce second-ring evidence

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput
no profiler/flamegraph evidence for the metrics loading path
no allocation audit (heaptrack/jemalloc) for the hot path
residual_risk: High: six BLOCKER findings remain unresolved, including three uses of unwrap() on fallible operations (I/O, parse, and implicit indexing), a lossy as cast, hidden I/O side effects, missing error types, and no functional core/shell separation. The code as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range value. Static review only — no commands were run.
